verdict.rationale: Windmill's user-token docs state that tokens can be scoped to specific resources and actions following least privilege, and a roles and permissions system is documented. Agents such as MCP clients can connect to Windmill, so scoped tokens are a direct way to grant an agent least-privilege access. missing for 10: detailed documentation of scope granularity and token issuance/expiry/revocation, explicit documentation tying scoped tokens to agent/MCP use, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: Tokens can be scoped to restrict access to specific resources and actions, following the principle of least privilege.
Windmill provides a roles and permissions system that allows you to control access and manage permissions within your instance and workspaces.
With MCP, you can connect your favorite LLMs (like Claude, Cursor, or any MCP compatible client) to Windmill, allowing you to trigger your scripts and flows from your client chat.
